layout_dets.text: Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Surface analysis methods such as AES, XPS and to a lesser extent SIMS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have been applied to the study of passive oxide films for a number of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: years and valuable information on chemical composition and film

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thickness has been obtained. A recent review of the literature (1)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shows, however, that published surface analysis data of passsive films

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: do not always agree, in particular those concerning the presence or not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of chloride ions in the films. Fig 1 gives a summary of published results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A better understanding of the composition of passive films on iron-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chromium alloys is of particular interest because of the practical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: importance of stainless steels as corrosion resistant alloys.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Molybdenum is a common alloying element in stainless steels. Its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: presence shifts the pitting potential to more noble values and thus

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: increases the resistance of the alloy to pitting corrosion. The reaction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mechanism of molybdenum is still not well known, however.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In our laboratory the surface analysis methods AES, XPS and SIMS are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: being used for the investigation of passive films on iron-chromium and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: iron-chromium-molybdenum alloys. The purpose of the present paper is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to investigate the influence of alloyed molybdenum on the distribution

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of chloride ions in the passive film of an iron-chromium model alloy.

layout_dets.text: Film thickness

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The film thickness was estimated from XPS data using deconvolution of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the metallic and oxide part of the Cr 2p3/2 peak (10,11). The results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: obtained for the two alloys polarised in the electrolytes (A) and (B) are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shown in Fig.6. The apparent film thickness is not significantly affected

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by the presence or not of chloride ion in the electrolyte or of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: molybdenum in the alloy. The film thickness of the samples that were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: during anodic passivation are only slightly thicker than the films

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Discussion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The analysis of chloride ion in passive films on iron-chromium alloys is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: very delicate because surface analytical data are easily obscured by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: artifacts. First of all, in presence of molybdenum AES can not be used

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reliably for the study of chloride profiles because of the interference

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: between the Ci 181 eV peak and the Mo 186 eV peak. On the other hand,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: XPS has a relatively low sensitivity for chloride. SIMS, in principle, is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: best suited but if used alone offers several difficulties of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interpretation (9). Indeed, measured SIMS intensities are heavily

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Passive films on FeCr and FeCrMo

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dependent on matrix effects and are not necessarily proportional to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: concentration of the element analysed. To avoid these difficulties

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: different methods were employed in the present study and all data were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interpreted based on relative measurments using the cathodically

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: polarised sample as a reference. The obtained results, therefore, are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: believed to be quite reliable.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The SIMS and AES data show that chloride is present in the passive film

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on the Fe24Cr alloy formed in the chloride containing electrolyte B. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shape of the chloride concentration profiles suggests that the chloride

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ions are situated in the outer part of the passive film, but distinctly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: deeper than adsorbed ions. The film formed on the Fe24Cr11Mo alloy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: apparently contains less chloride than that on Fe24Cr. The observed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: difference can perhaps explain the well known improvement of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stability of passive films on iron-chromium alloys by molybdenum but a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: detailed discussion of various hypotheses is beyond the scope of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: present paper.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The surface analysis methods used here give an average value over the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: analysed area rather than the local concentration on a microscopic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: level. It is, therefore, not possible from these data to decide whether

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the chloride ions are distributed uniformly on the analysed area or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: whether their presence is restricted to certain areas such as local

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: defects or micropores. The shape of the chloride profiles showing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: almost no chloride ion in the inner part of the film and at the film-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: metal interface seems to exclude that film rupture-repassivation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: events exposing briefly small parts of the bare metal surface are at the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: origin of the observed presence of chloride ions in the films.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Conclusions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: -Under the conditions of the present study the apparent thickness of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: passive film measured by XPS on Fe24Cr is not significantly affected by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the presence of chloride ion in the electrolyte or of molybdenum in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloy.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: -Passive films formed in the chloride containing electrolyte B on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fe24Cr contain more chloride than those formed under identical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: conditions on Fe24Cr11Mo.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: -The depth distribution of the chloride ions in the film is non uniform,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with a higher concentration in the outer part of the film.
